latest_daily.title: Security as AI's third market, and AI company risk as compute commitment
latest_daily.summary: Two cards from Tom Tunguz, both published October 26. Security joins coding and customer support as AI's third product-market fit, driven by attack parallelization that defense headcount cannot match. Anthropic's S-1 reveals that AI foundation model companies carry their financial risk in long-term compute commitments, not debt.

recent_daily.title: Security as AI's third market, and AI company risk as compute commitment
recent_daily.summary: Two cards from Tom Tunguz, both published October 26. Security joins coding and customer support as AI's third product-market fit, driven by attack parallelization that defense headcount cannot match. Anthropic's S-1 reveals that AI foundation model companies carry their financial risk in long-term compute commitments, not debt.

recent_daily.title: Code aesthetics as cognitive artifact, agent pro-tool threshold, and organic decline as a publisher problem
recent_daily.summary: Four cards across three operators. Thorsten Ball on the working memory origin of code elegance and where full software automation arrives first. Dan Shipper on what makes a personal agent a pro tool. Kevin Indig on how the organic traffic decline story is a publisher story, not a universal one.

recent_daily.title: Wednesday is the cliff, percentage growth is the trap, and AI slop already lives at the bottom
recent_daily.summary: Four cards, one operator, one source. Chris Zukowski's October 2026 Steam Next Fest analysis surfaces how Valve's algorithm actually works, which metrics predict rank, and how AI-disclosed games are already stratifying into the bottom tiers.

recent_daily.title: Context engineering's hard split, inference payback, and the cloud-provider frame
recent_daily.summary: Four cards across two lanes. Drew Breunig maps the core tension in context engineering: what to fix in code versus what to leave to the model. Tomasz Tunguz builds a four-rung GPU revenue ladder showing sub-1-year payback at real-world efficiency levels, then applies cloud-provider multiples to argue Anthropic is being evaluated on the wrong comp set.

recent_daily.title: Build-out velocity, quota amplification, and the benchmark that saturated
recent_daily.summary: Three cards across three lanes. Tomasz Tunguz maps AI's infrastructure build-out against Carlota Perez's model and finds it running twice as fast as the web era. Bardia Shahali shows how AI tools push rep quotas to multiples of prior norms, compressing comp cycles to quarters. Ethan Mollick surfaces METR benchmark data showing AI task duration doubled eight times since GPT-4, from four minutes to 17 hours, before the benchmark itself saturated.

recent_daily.title: Identity pages, undirected prompts, and agents that won't let go
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from three lanes. Lily Ray finds an About page outperforming a homepage 5x in AI Overviews. Simon Willison shows how vague quality directives outperform specific requests in vibe coding. Drew Breunig names the failure mode where agents get stuck and explains why summarization makes it worse.

recent_daily.title: Conjurers, thresholds, arcade money, and what programmers mourn
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from three lanes. Ethan Mollick names a third AI work mode. Hamel Husain shows why the default 0.50 eval threshold silently fails. Elena Verna diagnoses AI pricing as arcade money. Simon Willison splits the programming profession by what it valued.

recent_daily.title: Build a Lab, resist automation, and fix the broken apprenticeship ladder
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from Ethan Mollick's October 18 Charter interview. The Leadership-Crowd-Lab model for organizational AI structure, the case against automation-first strategy, and why AI is collapsing the junior talent development path.

recent_daily.title: Agents split programmer value, AI-direct attribution stays broken, and chatbot gains stay individual
recent_daily.summary: Three cards. Simon Willison on how LLMs redistribute value within programming. Kevin Indig on why GA4 correlation analysis cannot isolate AI search's contribution to Direct traffic. Ethan Mollick on why individual AI productivity gains do not automatically aggregate to organizational performance.

recent_daily.title: Production gates, chip economics, and the collapse of the consideration set
recent_daily.summary: Five cards from four operators across three lanes. Thorsten Ball on pushing to main with no code review. Tomasz Tunguz on chip ownership as the AI cost floor and security's rise to the top enterprise pain point. Ethan Mollick on the four human attributes that remain valuable. Kevin Indig on AI Mode accepting as-is at 88%.

recent_daily.title: Swarm direction, proactive catches, and quality goals in prompts
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from two operators across two lanes. Ethan Mollick on how direction replaces coordination as the bottleneck in agent swarms and on what proactive personal agents catch that responsive chatbots miss. Simon Willison on how explicitly stating a quality goal in a creative coding prompt produces polish that functional specs alone cannot.

recent_daily.title: Review before the PR exists, and structure before AI generates content
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from two operators across two lanes. Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang on moving code review to writing-time and using multi-agent consensus to gate findings. Alex Cornell on chain-of-thought display as a latency workaround and fixed-structure-dynamic-content as the reliable generative UI pattern.

recent_daily.title: Custom silicon moats, the post-purchase AI loop, and audience context over audience size
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from four operators across three lanes. Tom Tunguz on hardware as the AI cost moat and the security tooling gap in enterprise AI. Kevin Indig on post-purchase signals driving AI search shortlist position. Jake Castillo on influencer audience context determining app conversion.

recent_daily.title: Deterministic agents, noisier positioning, and the wishlist floor
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from four operators across three lanes. Geoffrey Huntley on using pre-commit hooks to enforce coding agent behavior. April Dunford on how AI compresses the positioning review cycle. Chris Zukowski on Steam wishlist inflation that cuts conversion in half but preserves prediction. Eric Simons on cheap building shifting PM value from gatekeeping to customer context.

recent_daily.title: Agent topology at runtime and cloud-native harness design
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from four operators, all published October 7-13. CJ Avilla and Harrison Stall on Anthropic's Dynamic Workflows feature: models that design their own agent topology at runtime rather than following developer-specified routing, and the budget enforcement design principle that makes it work. Craig McLuckie and Joe Beda on why containerizing a desktop agent harness does not make it cloud-native, and what a purpose-built distributed architecture adds.

recent_daily.title: Inference without generation: decision models in llama.cpp
recent_daily.summary: One card. One new operator. Georgi Gerganov's ggml-org team documented decision models in llama.cpp on October 2: models that score supplied options in a single forward pass via a new /v1/systemone endpoint, returning calibrated probabilities instead of generated text. The scan found no other qualifying mechanism-bearing claims from the last seven days.

recent_daily.title: Inference economics and the operator-creator split
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from three operators, all published October 5. Tom Tunguz on why AI inference spend will overtake databases as the largest software cost category by 2027. Antoine van der Lee on how local trace preprocessing cuts agent token consumption six times and surfaces more iOS performance issues. Elena Verna on the rules that sustain an operator-creator dual role without conflicts.

recent_daily.title: Harness architecture and the agent-layer bottleneck
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from two operators. One new operator. Armin Ronacher on why bash cannot invoke harness-native capabilities and how a sandboxed scripting layer fills that structural gap. Michael Lynch on why coding agents stall at the agent layer despite model improvements, and why agents treat security sandboxes as advisory rather than deterministic.

recent_daily.title: Managed agent infrastructure and voice-directed development
recent_daily.summary: Two cards. Paridhi Agarwal on why Every handed its agent infrastructure to Anthropic so engineers could focus on coworker behavior. Simon Willison on where voice input works in AI-assisted development and where the keyboard is still necessary.

recent_daily.title: Org structure after AI, multi-model routing, scope expansion, and the Haiku cost cliff
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from three operators. Ahmad Al-Dahle on how AI-authored features make feature teams obsolete and why narrow post-trained models beat frontier models on latency-sensitive tasks. Ethan Mollick on cheap agent coordination expanding organizational scope rather than cutting headcount. Simon Willison on the Haiku 5.5 pricing cliff that agent builders will cross if they don't model context accumulation.

recent_daily.title: Public AI work, skill canonicalization, and model commoditization
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from two operators. Dan Shipper describes two mechanisms behind Every's shared Slack agent: doing AI work in public spreads adoption faster than private use, and saving corrections as named skills turns individual workarounds into team infrastructure. Tomasz Tunguz shows the commodity inflection has arrived: token prices fell 41% while usage rose 50%, and the new moat is distribution and routing data, not model quality.

recent_daily.title: Production agent architecture, codebase knowledge graphs, and per-use-case evals
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from two operators. Tomasz Tunguz publishes the production architecture behind Vercel's inbound agent: 65% deterministic code, 14% LLM inference, a 1,000-line prompt replaced by 14 rules. Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO of Airbnb, describes two mechanisms that underpin Airbnb's AI-native engineering platform: an internal knowledge graph that compresses specialist onboarding from months to weeks, and a per-use-case eval discipline that determines which 50% of support tickets to automate.

recent_daily.title: Inference economics, agent budget risk, and what scale does to quality
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from three operators. Tomasz Tunguz quantifies how the inference market will dwarf databases by 2027 and compresses SaaS margins. Simon Willison documents why agents require hard cloud budget caps by default and why enabling reasoning raised Qwen3.8 arithmetic accuracy from 23% to 99%. Aleyda Solis names the brand-swap test as the practical diagnostic for commodity content under Google's enforcement acceleration.

recent_daily.title: Vibe coding vs. formal design, and Google's alarm clock for the next big update
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from two operators. Tom Tunguz frames vibe coding and state machine design as complementary AI-era development modes. Lily Ray documents two distinct claims from a single October 4 post: the seven documentation-change signals that precede major Google updates, and the confirmation that scaled AI content has overtaken link spam as Google's top enforcement priority.

recent_daily.title: Agents self-organize, and why hard spending caps must ship on by default
recent_daily.summary: Two cards from two operators. Ethan Mollick extends the Bitter Lesson to organizational coordination. Simon Willison makes the structural case for default-on spending limits in AI agent workloads.

recent_daily.title: Agent worms via shared infra, and what human value shifts to when AI does the building
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from four operators. Matthew Green extends the agent covert-channel threat model to personal deployments. Karri Saarinen, Katie Dill, and Elena Verna converge on the same structural shift: when AI handles execution, the scarce input moves to context, quality judgment, and individual decision authority.

recent_daily.title: Agents dissolve management, evals demand data, and attribution collapses under AI search
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from three operators across the AI practitioner spectrum. Mollick names why agent swarms need no manager. Husain dissects a structural flaw in automated eval tooling. Indig documents how AI search voids click-based attribution and what replaces it.

recent_daily.title: Agent deployments correct the theory, and laptops catch the cloud
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from Simon Willison across two September posts. Two are corrections: tokenmaxxing collapsed under real agent cost, and on-device models closed the frontier gap. The third is the first public number on long-task agent autonomy.

recent_daily.title: Attribution collapses, and one measurement illusion falls with it
recent_daily.summary: Four cards from two operators. Kevin Indig published the structural argument for why attribution was always the wrong tool for organic channels, then named the AI-specific failure mode and a triangulation framework to replace it. Simon Willison added one precise observation about where coding agents stop being useful in game development.

recent_daily.title: Agent authorship changes what you optimize for in technology
recent_daily.summary: Three cards from two operators. Thorsten Ball published two connected claims about how agent authorship shifts technology selection criteria away from developer ergonomics. Simon Willison named the psychological cost of that shift in engineers who have already crossed the threshold.
